catalog_snapshot.scope: accepted/pending/revision board records, repository PR metadata, and complete own-team history

selection_policy: Build the first objective that preserves a real industrial contact/alignment operation using only pinned public TaskFile primitives and the stock YAM action/scorer interfaces. Do not treat a material check, an IK plan, or a score of 1.0 as final task certification.

candidates.objective: With two arms, grasp a full-size short LM rail at two separated points, carry it onto its mounting base, and seat its marked reference side against the base side datum before temporary fastening.
candidates.industrial_operation: Initial datum seating of a linear-motion rail; the prototype ends before bolt insertion or torqueing.

source_evidence.locator: THK LM Guide Mounting Procedure, 'Mounting the LM Rail(s)', Fig. 7 text
source_evidence.support: THK instructs the installer to gently place the LM rail on the base and align the line-marked rail side with the base side reference surface.

source_evidence.locator: THK Mounting Procedure LM Guide, B1-89, Reference Surface Indicators
source_evidence.support: The official THK drawing identifies the line-marked side as the rail reference surface.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Slide a carriage onto a linear rail until it clicks
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: That task feeds a small carriage through a close-fitting T profile and detent. This objective transports the long rail itself with two grasp points and registers its side face to a machine datum; there is no carriage insertion or detent.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Lay a long DIN rail into both standoff cradles with two arms
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: This is the closest historical concept and must remain disclosed. Cradle placement constrains two discrete supports; the proposed THK operation registers a precision rail continuously against a planar side datum on its mounting base. Novelty still needs a later full similarity review.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Feed a hex shaft through two bearings
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: That task is axial insertion through two bores with regrasping. This is bimanual planar placement and side-datum seating with no bore insertion.

asset_runtime_feasibility.native_assets: One loose Box rail and fixed Box base/datum/stops; no compound rigid body, joint, deformable, mesh, or hidden constraint.
asset_runtime_feasibility.control: Stock yam_scripted policy, two simultaneous public Waypoint lists, 14-D absolute joint targets through the pinned embodiment.
asset_runtime_feasibility.scoring: TaskFile object pose/velocity only; final rail centre, height, yaw, side-datum gap, and rest state.
asset_runtime_feasibility.industrial_scale: 320 x 28 x 16 mm rail on a 380 x 150 mm base; not miniaturized metrology.
asset_runtime_feasibility.known_gap: The first GPU run must establish whether two independent parallel grippers can stably share this single rigid rail. Bolt-hole alignment and fastening are deliberately outside this prototype.

candidates.build_status: built-first; GPU execution intentionally delegated to trusted host

candidates.objective: Bimanually place a rigid machine table plate onto four pre-mounted LM blocks and register its datum edge before temporary fastening.
candidates.industrial_operation: Machine-table installation on linear guide blocks.

source_evidence.locator: THK LM Guide Mounting Procedure, 'Mounting the LM Blocks', Fig. 5 text
source_evidence.support: THK instructs the installer to gently place the table on the LM blocks, temporarily fasten it, and press the master-side blocks to the table reference surface.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Lay a long DIN rail into both standoff cradles with two arms
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: Both require bimanual long-part support, but this objective registers one broad table over four distributed LM blocks rather than laying a rail into two cradles.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Slide a carriage onto a linear rail until it clicks
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: This is a table-to-four-block mating operation, not a carriage-on-profile insertion.

asset_runtime_feasibility.prototype_kind: material design only in this experiment
asset_runtime_feasibility.native_assets: A loose Box plate and four fixed Box blocks are representable.
asset_runtime_feasibility.control: A two-point bimanual Waypoint plan is possible with stock YAM.
asset_runtime_feasibility.blocking_risk: With plain boxes, the four blocks provide only support surfaces and do not preserve the real LM-block/table fastener registration. Building it now would collapse the objective toward generic plate placement.

candidates.build_status: not built; held behind build-first candidate pending a supported registration feature

candidates.objective: Inspect a finished threaded robot part with the GO and NO-GO ends of a thread limit gauge, accepting free GO travel and no more than three NO-GO turns.
candidates.industrial_operation: Post-finish functional inspection of thread pitch/diameter using a threaded plug or ring gauge.

source_evidence.locator: Thorlabs Mechanical Standards SQ-PO-001 Rev 2.0, page 2 anodizing requirement 3(a), and page 3 Gauging Techniques 5(c)
source_evidence.support: The standard requires finished threads to remain within major/minor/pitch diameter specifications and states the GO free-spin and three-turn NO-GO procedures.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Sort machined blocks with a go/no-go gap gauge
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: That task classifies block width by gravity seating in two linear gaps. Thread gauging tests coupled axial/rotational engagement and turn count, but it remains close in the broader limit-gauging family.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Set a telescoping gauge to a bearing housing's bore diameter and leave it on its stand
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: That task captures an internal diameter through sprung radial contact and lock retention. Thread gauging is a functional helical fit test.

closest_catalog_comparisons.title: Start a hex nut on a stud the trained way
closest_catalog_comparisons.meaningful_difference: That concept is assembly/cross-thread avoidance; this is dimensional acceptance with two calibrated limit members.

asset_runtime_feasibility.blocking_risk: The public TaskFile has no joint hook or helical constraint. Plain cylinders would turn this into relabelled insertion, while task-local thread contact would introduce untested microscopic/helical physics. It is also too close to existing limit-gauge work to justify that risk.

candidates.build_status: not built; exact physics and novelty blockers recorded
